title: How a Piano Works in 60 Seconds 🎹🔨 #shorts
description:
A piano is a percussion instrument: every key throws a felt hammer at steel strings. About 230 strings pull on a cast-iron frame with around 18 tons of tension. An escapement lets the hammer bounce right off so the string can ring, and a damper stops it when you let go. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#piano #music #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: Inside a piano, about *230 strings* pull with nearly *18 tons* of force.

steps.label: Key
steps.text: A key is a *lever*. Press the front, and the back end *lifts up*.

steps.label: Hammer
steps.text: That throws a *felt hammer* up at the strings. A piano is really a *percussion* instrument.

steps.label: Escapement
steps.text: The *escapement* lets the hammer *bounce right off*, so the string can ring freely.

steps.label: Soundboard
steps.text: The string's vibration flows into a big wooden *soundboard*, which makes it *loud*.

steps.label: Damper
steps.text: Let go of the key, and a felt *damper* drops on the string and *stops the sound*.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Lever, hammer, *string*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
